terms.gloss: a written message on a phone
terms.comment: Andresian’s phrase, paired with nūntius vōcālis for a voicemail: a message one reads, against one that is heard. Traupman (p. 261) gives nūntius for a message on a computer. To text someone is nūntium (scrīptum) alicui mittere.
Cicero’s word for a hasty little letter, which suits a few lines sent from a phone.

phrases.latin: hoc litterulārum exarāvī ēgrediēns ē vīllā ante lūcem
phrases.english: I scribbled this little note as I was leaving the house before dawn

sources: Lewis & Short: nuntius · Lewis & Short: scriptus · Lewis & Short: litterula
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 261.
